result.title: mmTherm: Absolute 3D Human Pose Estimation from Low-Resolution Thermal Images and mmWave Radar
result.summary: Absolute 3D human pose estimation (HPE) aims to recover both a person's body pose and their global position in 3D space. Privacy-preserving millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar provides distance and direction measurement capabilities, but its sparse point clouds make HPE under-constrained. Low-resolution thermal imaging can provide complementary observations of body direction and structure. However, our evaluation shows that a strong feature-level fusion baseline loses much of its localization and HPE advantage when generalizing to unseen subjects, with radial localization becoming less accurate than a radar-only baseline. Motivated by this finding, we introduce mmTherm, a lightweight framework that explicitly incorporates the complementary geometric properties of thermal imaging and mmWave radar. It combines body structure and joint directions estimated from thermal images with range information from radar to localize the body and reconstruct its 3D pose. Experiments on OctoNet show that mmTherm reduces cross-user absolute joint error by 33% and root localization error by 38% relative to the strongest corresponding baselines, while requiring substantially fewer parameters and less computation at inference.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作研究低分辨率热成像与毫米波雷达联合的绝对 3D 人体姿态估计，发现强特征级融合在跨被试泛化时反而丧失定位优势，转而显式结合热成像给出的身体结构与关节方向与雷达测距来完成定位与姿态重建。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「端到端特征融合在新分布下退化、改为保留显式几何中间量」的现象，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据在 latent 状态中坍缩、以及显式结构化中间表示的设计问题是同类问题，可供核查，但领域相隔较远。
